mcq_choices.rationale: Assumes adding inert gas raises the partial pressures of the reacting gases, but at constant volume their moles and pressures are unaffected.
Assumes the added inert gas dilutes the reacting gases, but at constant volume each species' partial pressure depends only on its own moles and volume.
Assumes the inert gas selectively affects only reactants, but reactant and product partial pressures are each set independently by their own moles and volume.

mcq_choices.choice_text: the reacting-gas partial pressures do not change
mcq_choices.rationale: fixed component moles, volume, and temperature leave partial pressures unchanged

parts.prompt:
Adding an inert gas at constant volume to an ideal-gas equilibrium changes equilibrium because

A. all partial pressures increase
B. all partial pressures decrease
C. reactant partial pressures alone increase
D. the reacting-gas partial pressures do not change

criteria.description: Select the single scientifically correct answer.
required_evidence: fixed component moles, volume, and temperature leave partial pressures unchanged
